Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
915 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes made this morning to the forecast. After
coordination, decision made to not issue a fire weather SPS for
today. See fire weather section below for more details.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Rain returns Thursday as colder temperatures follow Friday
     into the weekend, with mountain snow and brisk conditions.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Rain returns Thursday as colder temperatures follow 
Friday into the weekend, with mountain snow and brisk conditions.

Shortwave ridging coupled with westerly downslope flow will
allow for mild afternoons today and Wednesday. High temperatures
today will be around 70. Wednesday will be a few degs cooler 
due to more clouds and lighter SE winds. Very dry today with 
marginal fire weather concerns. See Fire Weather section below. 

Rain is expected to move in by early Thursday as low pressure
crosses the Appalachians and over to the Mid-Atlantic coast.
There weren't any significant changes seen at the sfc or at  
500 mb compared to previous runs with the system expected to 
impact the area Thursday into Friday.

Behind this system, much colder air will follow on brisk NNW
winds with the Allegheny Mountains seeing their first 
accumulating snow of the season starting late Thu night and 
continuing through Fri evening. A few inches of accumulation are
likely falling roughly in a 24-hr period from 06Z Fri through
06Z Sat. 

Remaining colder than normal Fri through the first half of next
week under brisk NNW flow between low pressure well offshore and
strong Canadian high pressure to our west.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Lighter winds today than yesterday, but potentially still 
gusting 15-20 kt range during the afternoon. Winds shift to the
southeast Wed with even lighter speeds.

Rain is expected to arrive by daybreak Thu and continue through
the day before it starts exiting to the northeast Thu night, but
may linger into Fri morning across northeast Maryland. 

Brisk NNW winds gusting 20-30 kt will be the biggest impact
Fri-Sun. MVFR/IFR conditions are likely Thursday into Fri
morning with a broken stratocu layer persisting all weekend into
early next week.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds remain generally below SCA through Thursday. Winds
strengthen Thu night through the weekend and peak in strength
Saturday with SCA conditions expected Thu night through at least
the first part of next week. A period of gale force winds is
possible Saturday due to tight pressure gradient between deep
low offshore and strong Canadian high pressure over the MS River
Valley.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Fire weather conditions could be locally sensitive today given
the well above normal temperatures and minimum RH values in the
25 to 35 percent range. Winds are going to be lighter than
yesterday, with gusts around 15-20 mph at times. The Potomac
Highlands and northern Shenandoah Valley are the main areas to
closely monitor, but overall conditions are marginal so have 
opted not to issue a fire weather SPS today.
